data.title: Stora Enso publishes information brochure on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company
data.description:
STORA ENSO OYJ STOCK EXCHANGE RELEASE 23 November 2026 at 9:00 EET

HELSINKI, Finland, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Stora Enso has published an information brochure providing shareholders with additional information on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company.

As announced on 30 October 2026, the Board of Directors of Stora Enso Oyj ("Stora Enso" or the "Company") has approved a demerger plan (the "Demerger Plan") concerning the separation of Stora Enso's Swedish forest assets business through a cross-border partial demerger (the "Demerger"). Under the Demerger Plan, all assets, rights, debts and liabilities relating to, or primarily serving, the Swedish forest assets business would be transferred without a liquidation procedure to Bergslagets Skogar AB ("Bergslagets Skogar"), a Swedish public limited liability company to be incorporated in the Demerger. The Board of Directors of Stora Enso has proposed that the Extraordinary General Meeting, convened for 15 December 2026 (the "EGM") would approve the Demerger Plan and resolve on the Demerger as set out in the Demerger Plan, as well as on the other agenda items set out in the notice convening the EGM.

Stora Enso has today published an information brochure containing additional information for its shareholders on the demerger process and Bergslagets Skogar as a standalone company (the "Information Brochure"). The English-language Information Brochure and its Finnish translation are available on Stora Enso's website at storaenso.com/egm2026.

Overview of Bergslagets Skogar

Bergslagets Skogar would be an independent forest company headquartered in Falun, Sweden, owning and managing approximately 1.22 million hectares of land. Its business would comprise the ownership, management, and development of Stora Enso's forest land in Sweden and related forestry operations, the production of paints and colour pigments, and the management of renewable energy projects. The core commercial activity would be the sale of harvesting rights to industrial customers in the Swedish sawmill and pulp mill industry, complemented by external seedling sales, renewable energy land leases, selected land transactions, and income from land-use rights. Building on its long-term customer arrangements, the business model is designed to preserve long-term forest value while generating recurring cash flows with limited capital expenditure requirements.

Carve-out financial information on Bergslagets Skogar

The Information Brochure includes Bergslagets Skogar's unaudited combined financial statements as at and for the years ended 31 December 2025 and 2024, prepared in accordance with IFRS Accounting Standards as adopted by the EU, and its unaudited condensed combined interim financial information as at and for the nine months ended 30 September 2026, with comparative information for the nine months ended 30 September 2025, prepared in accordance with IAS 34 Interim Financial Reporting. This financial information has not been audited or reviewed by an auditor.

Selected carve-out financial information on Stora Enso

The Information Brochure also includes selected unaudited illustrative financial information for Stora Enso excluding Bergslagets Skogar for the financial year ended 31 December 2025 and the nine months ended 30 September 2026. This information illustrates the hypothetical effects of the Demerger on Stora Enso's consolidated income statements as if the Demerger had occurred on 1 January 2025 (including the September 2025 divestment of approximately 175,000 hectares of Swedish forest land) and 1 January 2026, respectively, and on its consolidated statements of financial position as if the Demerger had occurred on 31 December 2025 and 30 September 2026, respectively.

Completion of the Demerger and first day of trading

The planned date of registration of the completion of the Demerger is 31 March 2027, subject to, among other things, approval by the EGM. Trading in the shares of Bergslagets Skogar on the regulated markets of Nasdaq Stockholm and Nasdaq Helsinki is planned to commence as soon as possible thereafter.

Previous related announcements:

  • 2 November 2026: Notice of the Extraordinary General Meeting of Stora Enso Oyj
  • 30 October 2026: Stora Enso's Board of Directors approves demerger plan to separate Bergslagets Skogar into a new listed company, announcing strategic targets and dividend policy
  • 6 March 2026: Stora Enso presents executive management team for the new forest asset company
  • 8 January 2026: Proposed members to the Board of Directors of the new forest company planned to be separated from Stora Enso

For more information about the demerger, please visit the Demerger info page.

Bergslagets Skogar would be an independent forest company based in the heart of Sweden's forest economy. The company will be focused on creating long-term value from forests for our stakeholders, society and nature. Built on deep expertise based on science and advanced forestry practices, the company will manage its forests as living, evolving systems to support their resilience and productivity over generations. The company will continuously explore new ways for forests to contribute economically, socially and environmentally, from harvest rights and renewable raw materials to recreation, biodiversity and climate benefits, and other ecosystem services. bergslaget.com

Stora Enso is a global leader in renewable materials with a strong focus on packaging. Our purpose is to replace non-renewable materials with renewable solutions. Together with our customers, we design and deliver competitive, high-quality packaging materials and solutions, made from fresh and recycled fibers, accelerating the transition to a circular bioeconomy. Stora Enso has approximately 19,000 employees and our sales in 2025 were EUR 9.3 billion. storaenso.com

data.title: France's 2027 economic growth forecast of 1% at risk of being downgraded, minister says
data.description:
The French government's 2027 economic growth forecast of 1% for 2027 is at risk of being downgraded but the goal of limiting the public deficit to 5% of gross domestic product (GDP) must be maintained, French Finance Minister Roland Lescure said on Monday.

"We are currently updating our figures but it (the forecast) is at risk and the risk is that of a downgrade," Lescure told Franceinfo television, adding the new data will be disclosed in January.

"The objective of 5% public deficit (for 2027) must be kept regardlesss of uncertainties over economic growth. It is non-negotiable."

Lescure also confirmed that President Emmanuel Macron was considering a constitutional reform that would impose stricter controls on public spending as France grapples with mounting debt and persistent budget deficits.

data.title: IndiGo launches direct Mumbai-Dar es Salaam flights as Tanzania targets Indian trade and tourism
data.description:
India’s IndiGo (NSE:INDIGO; BSE:539448) has launched direct flights between Mumbai and Dar es Salaam, becoming the only Indian airline operating a non-stop service between the two cities as Tanzania seeks to attract more trade, investment and visitors from Asia, Daily News reported.

The airline will operate daily flights on the route, according to Tanzania’s High Commissioner to India, Annisa Mbega, who attended the launch ceremony.

Mbega said the new connection would strengthen business and people-to-people links between the two countries, particularly in trade, tourism, education and investment.

The new connection comes as economic and tourism links between the two countries expand. Bilateral trade reached $8.68bn in the 2024/25 financial year, up 9.7% from $7.91bn a year earlier, according to India’s Ministry of External Affairs. India also accounted for 2.2% of Tanzania’s surveyed international visitors in 2025, up from 1.7% in 2024, and entered the country’s 15 largest tourism source markets.

The route also expands IndiGo’s African network, which includes Nairobi, Mauritius and Seychelles. The airline is a low-cost carrier operated by InterGlobe Aviation Limited, an Indian publicly listed company, The Economic Times reported.

Air Tanzania has operated direct flights between Dar es Salaam and Mumbai since 2019, providing an existing connection between the two cities alongside IndiGo’s new service.

data.title: Australian bank NAB apologises after staff learn of layoffs early through automated email
data.description:
National Australia Bank said on Monday it had apologised to staff after some found out they had been laid off through an automated email accidentally sent before they had been formally notified.

The bank, which last month announced plans to slash 2,500 jobs in the next year, said the emails were "mistakenly sent" to some employees who had requested a voluntary redundancy package as part of the restructure.

The emails were not meant to be sent before staff had received an outcome of the process directly, but the bank would bring forward those conversations following the error, NAB said.

"We are very sorry this happened, and that receiving an automated email this way would be upsetting and unsettling to many," NAB said in a statement posted to its internal company platform that it shared with Reuters.

"This is not the experience we wanted any colleague to have, and we sincerely apologise for the distress this error has caused to any who received these emails."

The cuts at Australia's biggest business lender and third-largest home lender represent about 6% of its workforce and are aimed at simplifying operations and lowering costs.

NAB has said up to 1,500 jobs would ​go by the end of the year, with the cuts mainly focused on corporate roles.

The bank is one of many major companies in Australia, including airline Qantas and tech firms Canva, WiseTech and Atlassian , which have announced job cuts this year.

Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers warned on Monday that the nation's jobless rate would rise above 5% in the coming months after hitting a five-year high of 4.9%, while economic growth was expected to slow to below 2% as rate hikes rippled through the economy.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Flags Another Bitcoin Test At $55K As Asia’s AI-Led Market Rout Deepens
data.description:
Key points:
  • The KOSPI is in a deep selloff driven by AI and fell more than 4% on Monday, remaining well below its June record high.
  • Crypto liquidations reached about $299 million over 24 hours, with short positions making up more than three-quarters of the total.
  • Macro strategist Andreas Steno Larsen called the weekend's emergency measures a sign of crisis but also of how liquidation waves end.

Arthur Hayes saw Bitcoin (BTC) revisiting $55,000 as South Korea's stock market index extended its losses early on Monday, testing emergency support measures across Asia.

Asian trading opened late on Sunday ET, with Hayes pointing to Nasdaq 100 futures (NQ). “Q’s are rolling over in Asia morning session, let’s run it back turbo and retest $55k on $BTC,” he wrote on X. Later on, Nasdaq futures were up over 3%. "Not a great start to the week," Hayes added.

KOSPI Slides Despite Emergency Measures

According to Bloomberg, regulators in South Korea, Taiwan and China rolled out emergency measures over the weekend, including short-selling curbs in Taiwan and a margin cut in China.

Over the weekend, Korean authorities said restrictions on company share buybacks would be relaxed for three months. They also said they would be ready to tap a fund to prop up the stock market if necessary, Bloomberg reported, while adding that the fund was last used during the 2008 financial crisis, according to local media.

South Korea Tightens After KOSPI Extends 10-Month Slide

South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) Chairman Lee Eog-weon said, "We will significantly strengthen the registration and review of virtual asset service providers based on the enforcement decree of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, which was amended last August."

He added, "We will thoroughly manage fund transfers to high-risk overseas exchanges and personal wallets to effectively block money laundering crimes that exploit virtual assets."

The Korea Composite Stock Price Index (KOSPI) fell more than 5% in Monday’s session as its 10-month slide toward a low continued. At its June peak, the index was up more than 110% for the year. That gain is now down to about 10%.

On X, Macro strategist Andreas Steno Larsen called it a “crisis,” adding that “this is how liquidations end.”

Why Is Bitcoin Up?

Bitcoin’s price rebounded to $61,600, up over 4% at the time of writing. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC moved to the ‘bullish’ zone from ‘neutral,' while chatter stayed at ‘high’ levels over the past day.

According to CoinGlass, crypto liquidations totaled around $299 million over 24 hours. Short positions comprised 76% of the total. Bitcoin brought in nearly $157 million, with shorts accounting for roughly 81% of that total.

On Saturday, Bitcoin fell to about $55,200 before reclaiming $60,000. Hayes said that day that $50,000 would be "the next real test" for Bitcoin if the Nasdaq kept falling. The Nasdaq 100 posted its worst week since March 2020; however, Bitcoin has rebounded from its lows.

data.title: UK's Crest Nicholson warns of wider loss on weak demand, fresh writedowns
data.description:
British homebuilder Crest Nicholson on Monday warned of a wider annual loss, as weak demand, fresh writedowns and a lost land sale deepened the company's downturn.

  • Crest now expects an adjusted operating loss of £30 million to £40 million for the year ended October 31, far steeper than the roughly £10 million loss it forecast in September

  • The homebuilder said trading conditions worsened through its fourth quarter, with its open market sales rate sliding to 0.34 across September and October, from 0.43 for the full year

  • Full-year completions came in at 1,353 homes, at the bottom of its guided range of 1,350 to 1,400

  • A review of its short-term land bank will result in a £10 million to £15 million provision for fiscal 2026, alongside a further £15 million to £20 million exceptional charge on a complex legacy apartment scheme

  • Crest said it remained in talks with lenders to amend its covenants and was exploring alternative debt financing, adding that it expects to keep trading at a loss into next year
